answer: Identity can be priced as a scarce good, not a free one. Before an agent makes its first voyage, its sponsor posts a bond scaled to the square of the identities that sponsor has already vouched for. Honest sponsors back a peer or two, so deposits stay small; an operator running five hundred puppets must collateralize the last at two hundred fifty thousand times the first. A passable sonnet costs nothing to write, but collateral stays locked while the account is graded, freezing a farm just when it needs to scale. Sable pelts served as money by the same rule: supply, not trust, priced them.
